summary: 为类人猿争取基本法律权利的运动已影响部分政策。文章梳理支持理由、反对者对权利范围的担心及双方的回应。
logic: 类人猿基本权利的倡议与政策进展
支持者为何主张扩大权利
权利边界和医学研究引发的争论
人与其他动物之间的法律界线

paragraphs.brief: 给予大猩猩 — — 我们最近的动物亲戚，包括黑猩猩、大猩猩、猩猩和慈善家 — — 基本合法权利的要求近几十年来越来越强烈。
sentences: Calls to grant basic legal rights to great apes – our closest animal relatives, including chimpanzees, gorillas, orangutans, and bonobos – have been growing louder in recent decades.
给予大猩猩 — — 我们最近的动物亲戚，包括黑猩猩、大猩猩、猩猩和慈善家 — — 基本合法权利的要求近几十年来越来越强烈。

Proponents of this movement argue that because great apes share so many genetic, cognitive, and emotional similarities with humans, they deserve fundamental rights such as the right to life, freedom, and protection from torture.
这场运动的支持者认为，由于巨猿与人类有着许多遗传、认知和情感上的相似之处，他们理应享有生命权、自由权和免受酷刑的权利等基本权利。
These advocates, notably philosophers like Peter Singer, point out that there is “no sound moral reason” to limit basic rights only to members of our own species.
这些倡导者，特别是Peter Singer等哲学家指出，“没有合理的道德理由”将基本权利仅限于我们自己的种族成员。
In 1993, Singer and others launched the Great Ape Project (GAP) with the aim of securing a “community of equals” in which human and non-human great apes alike enjoy these basic rights.
1993年，Singer和其他人发起了大猩猩项目，目的是确保一个“平等社区”，使人类和非人类的巨猿都能享有这些基本权利。

paragraphs.brief: 自1990年代以来，大型猿权利运动取得了一些具体的里程碑。
sentences: Since the 1990s, the great ape rights movement has achieved some concrete milestones.
自1990年代以来，大型猿权利运动取得了一些具体的里程碑。

For example, in 1999 New Zealand enacted an amendment to its Animal Welfare Act that, while stopping short of full “legal personhood” for apes, effectively banned invasive research, testing or teaching involving great apes.
例如，1999年，新西兰颁布了《动物福利法》修正案，在停止对猿类完全 " 法律人格 " 的同时，有效禁止涉及巨猿的侵入性研究、测试或教学。
This made New Zealand one of the first countries to extend special legal protections to non-human hominids, granting great apes more protection than any other animals had at the time.
这使新西兰成为第一批向非人类人类提供特别法律保护的国家之一，给予大猩猩的保护比当时任何其他动物都多。
Similarly, in 2008 Spain’s parliament became the first national legislature to formally endorse the Great Ape Project’s principles.
同样，2008年，西班牙议会成为正式认可大猩猩项目原则的第一个国家立法机构。
The Spanish environmental committee approved a resolution urging recognition of great apes’ rights to life and freedom.
西班牙环境委员会批准了一项决议，敦促承认巨猿的生命和自由权利。
This led to plans to outlaw harmful experiments on apes, ban their use in circuses or TV commercials, and improve conditions for apes kept in zoos.
这导致计划取缔对猿的有害实验，禁止在马戏团或电视广告中使用，并改善动物园内对猿的害害条件。
Pedro Pozas, the Spanish director of GAP, hailed it as “a historic day in the struggle for animal rights…in defense of our evolutionary comrades.”
“类人猿计划”西班牙负责人佩德罗·波萨斯称，这是“为动物权利而奋斗、为我们在进化上的近亲争取权益的历史性一天”。

paragraphs.brief: 根据这一逻辑，将基本权利扩大到其他聪明、有见识的人，仅仅是“道德圈的扩大”，超越了人类。
sentences: Why great apes?
为什么是大猩猩？
Advocates argue that great apes experience a rich emotional and social life much like humans.
倡导者认为，伟大的猿类经历丰富的情感和社会生活与人类相似。
They form long-term family bonds, show grief at the death of loved ones, use primitive language and tools, and demonstrate self-awareness and empathy.
它们形成长期的家庭纽带，对亲人的死亡表示悲痛，使用原始语言和工具，并展示自我意识和同情心。
In Singer’s view, these capacities mean apes “deserve the same consideration humans extend to members of our own species.”
在Singer看来，这些能力意味着猿类 " 值得人类对自身物种成员给予同样的考虑。

Even if apes cannot reciprocate or participate in human society at our level, supporters say that is morally irrelevant – after all, human infants or severely disabled individuals still have rights, and “if we were to meet intelligent extraterrestrials, would we deny them rights just because they’re not Homo sapiens?”
即使猿类不能对我们作出回报或参与人类社会，支持者也说这在道德上是无关紧要的 — — 毕竟，人类婴儿或严重残疾者仍然有权利，而且“如果我们遇到聪明的外星人，我们是否会仅仅因为他们不是智人而剥夺他们的权利？”
By this logic, extending basic rights to other intelligent, sentient beings is simply an “expansion of the moral circle” beyond humanity.
根据这一逻辑，将基本权利扩大到其他聪明、有见识的人，仅仅是“道德圈的扩大”，超越了人类。

Singer and his colleagues coined the term “speciesism” for the prejudice of favoring one’s own species over others; they condemn this bias as akin to racism or sexism, arguing that shared sentience and intelligence, not species membership, should be the basis for moral rights.
歌手和他的同事用“物种”一词来形容偏向于自己种族的偏见；他们谴责这种偏见，认为这种偏见类似于种族主义或性别歧视，认为共同的感性与智慧，而不是物种成员，应该是道德权利的基础。
sectionTitle: 支持类人猿权利的理由

paragraphs.brief: 此外，许多GAP支持者认为巨猿只是向更广泛的动物保护迈出的第一步。
sentences: Furthermore, many GAP supporters see great apes as just the first step toward broader animal protection.
此外，许多GAP支持者认为巨猿只是向更广泛的动物保护迈出的第一步。
They chose apes because the ethical case is especially strong – apes are so close to us – and thus more likely to gain public support.
他们选择猿类是因为伦理学上的情况特别严重 — — 猿类离我们如此近 — — 因而更有可能获得公众的支持。

“The GAP is not a plea to save endangered animals or for better treatment,” Singer explains, “it is a call to respect the rights of individual animals…a first breach in the species barrier that could, in time, extend to other non-humans.”
GAP并不是要拯救濒危动物或寻求更好的治疗”，Singer 解释道，“这是要求尊重个别动物的权利... 第一次突破物种屏障，最终会延伸到其他非人类。

In other words, giving gorillas and chimps basic rights would be an unprecedented legal breakthrough, one that implicitly recognizes that some non-human animals are entitled to the same legal consideration as humans.
换句话说，给予大猩猩和黑猩猩基本权利将是一个前所未有的法律突破，它意味着承认一些非人类动物有权得到与人类相同的法律考虑。

paragraphs.brief: (实际上，大赦国际西班牙分部对《性别行动计划》的建议作出了回应，指出 " 人类的权利尚未得到充分保障 "。)
sentences: Not everyone agrees with this radical idea.
不是每个人都同意这种激进的想法。
Critics of great ape rights argue that we should not extend rights beyond our own species.
对大猩猩权利的批评者认为，我们不应该将权利扩大到我们自己的物种之外。
They often point out that even among humans, many people still lack full human rights, so our focus should remain on protecting human rights first.
他们经常指出，即使在人类中，许多人仍然缺乏充分的人权，因此，我们的重点应该仍然是首先保护人权。
(Indeed, Amnesty International’s Spanish branch responded to the GAP proposal by noting that “humans have yet to see their rights fully guaranteed”.)
(实际上，大赦国际西班牙分部对《性别行动计划》的建议作出了回应，指出 " 人类的权利尚未得到充分保障 "。)
Some view the campaign as misguided or even absurd – one Spanish archbishop famously complained that “only a ridiculous or distorted society” would grant human-like rights to apes.
有些人认为这场运动是误导甚至荒谬的 — — 一位西班牙大主教大肆抱怨说，“只有荒谬或扭曲的社会”才会赋予猿类类似人权。
These opponents warn that blurring the once-clear line between humans and other animals could devalue human dignity or create a slippery slope of claims from “all sorts of creatures”.
这些反对者警告说，模糊人类与其他动物之间一度明确的界线，会降低人的尊严的价值，或造成“各种生物”的主张滑坡。

paragraphs.brief: 如果我们给黑猩猩权利怀疑论者会问其它像大象或海豚这样的聪明动物呢？
sentences: In fact, the “slippery slope” argument is a common theme.
事实上，“滑坡”的论点是一个共同的主题。
If we give chimps rights, skeptics ask, what about other intelligent animals like elephants or dolphins?
如果我们给黑猩猩权利怀疑论者会问其它像大象或海豚这样的聪明动物呢？
Where do we stop?
我们该在哪停车？
They worry that granting personhood to apes “may pave the way for the extension of rights to all primates, or all mammals, or all sentient beings.”
他们担心给予猿类人格“可能为所有灵长类动物或所有哺乳动物，或所有有感性的生物的权利铺平了道路”。
Even some animal welfare supporters are uneasy about this.
甚至一些动物福利支持者都对此感到不安。
In the Time magazine coverage of Spain’s decision, a bullfighting advocate agreed apes should be protected from abuse, “but when you start equating animals with humans, it’s a slippery slope.”
在《时代》杂志报道西班牙的决定时，斗牛运动的倡导者同意保护猩猩不受虐待，“但是当你开始将动物与人类等同起来时，这是一个滑坡。”
He feared it “could eventually lead” to calls for rights for other animals (tongue-in-cheek, “bull rights” for Spain’s bulls) – a prospect he opposed.
他担心这“最终会引领”其他动物的权利呼吁(即西班牙公牛的“捆绑权 ” )，他反对这一前景。

paragraphs.brief: 同样，著名的动物权利理论家Gary Francione法律教授原则上支持更广泛的“滑坡坡”。
sentences: Peter Singer’s reply to this objection is essentially: so what?
Peter Singer对此异议的反应基本上是：那又怎样？
He acknowledges that ape rights could set a precedent for other animals – “They [critics] could be right.
他承认猿的权利可以为其他动物开创一个先例 — — “它们[批评人]可能是对的。
Only time will tell,” he says – but that is no reason to reject the idea.
他说：只有时间才能说明问题，但没有理由拒绝这个想法。
“We should not be deterred from doing what is right now by the fear that we may later be persuaded to do what is right again.”
“我们不应因为担心以后会再次被说服做正确的事情而不敢做现在该做的事。”
In other words, if extending rights to other deserving creatures follows logically, we ought to embrace that progression, not fear it.
换句话说，如果将权利扩大到其他值得保护的生物顺理成章，我们就应该接受这种进步，而不是害怕它。
Likewise, law professor Gary Francione, a prominent animal rights theorist, actually supports the broader “slippery slope” in principle.
同样，著名的动物权利理论家Gary Francione法律教授原则上支持更广泛的“滑坡坡”。
Francione argues that all sentient beings (not just great apes) “deserve to be free from exploitation,” since any being capable of feeling pain or pleasure has an interest in not suffering.
Francione认为，所有有天赋的生物(不仅仅是大猩猩)“都有资格免受剥削”，因为任何能够感到痛苦或快乐的人都有兴趣不遭受痛苦。
In his view, focusing only on apes is arbitrary; he calls the exclusion of other feeling animals morally unjustifiable.
他认为，只注重猿类是任意的；他称排除其他有道德上不合理的感觉的动物。
Francione even criticizes the Great Ape Project for what he calls “similar minds” bias – granting rights to apes because they resemble us, rather than because of their sentience alone.
弗朗西昂甚至批评大猩猩计划(Great Ape Project)所谓的“相似的思想”偏见 — — 给予猿类权利是因为它们长得像我们，而不是仅仅因为他们的灵性。
Still, Francione and Singer share the same ultimate goal of ending the property status of animals; they differ mainly on strategy (whether to start with apes or advocate for all animals at once).
然而，弗朗索内和辛格有着结束动物财产状况的同样最终目标；它们主要在战略上(无论是从猿类开始还是同时倡导所有动物)有所不同。

paragraphs.brief: 他们声称，给予猿类权利会模糊人类-动物的边界，并可能破坏科学进步。
sentences: Another concern is practical impact on science.
另一个关切是对科学的实际影响。
Some scientists worry that giving legal rights or personhood to apes could undermine valuable medical research and complicate how we treat animals in captivity.
一些科学家担心，给予猿类合法权利或人格可能会损害宝贵的医学研究，使我们对待被囚禁动物的方式复杂化。
In the 1980s and 90s, research on chimpanzees contributed to studies on diseases like AIDS and hepatitis.
在1980年代和90年代，对黑猩猩的研究促进了对艾滋病和肝炎等疾病的研究。
Opponents of an outright ban argued that in a public health emergency (say, a new lethal virus), researchers “may need to use chimps, orangutans or even gorillas” to find a cure.
反对彻底禁止的人认为，在公共卫生紧急情况下(比如，一种新的致命病毒)，研究人员“可能需要使用黑猩猩、猩猩甚至大猩猩来寻找治愈方法”。
They also argue that humans have a unique moral status necessary for ethical research boundaries.
他们还认为，人类具有道德研究界限所必须的独特道德地位。
Granting rights to apes blurs the human–animal boundary, they claim, and could hamstring scientific progress.
他们声称，给予猿类权利会模糊人类-动物的边界，并可能破坏科学进步。

For instance, Colin Blakemore, a prominent British neuroscientist, felt “not entirely comfortable” with a total ban on ape experiments and worried about “where the moral boundaries lie” if we treat apes almost like humans.
例如，英国知名神经科学家科林·布莱克莫尔认为，完全禁止子实验"并不完全舒服"，并且担心如果我们对子几乎像人类一样对待"道德界限"

paragraphs.brief: Singer在2006年指出，“欧洲目前没有对大猩猩进行医学研究”，因为欧盟(荷兰)唯一的黑猩猩实验室因没有必要而刚刚关闭。
sentences: However, supporters counter that this worry is largely outdated.
然而，支持者反驳说，这种担心基本上已经过时。
In practice, using great apes in research has already been in decline for decades.
在实践中，研究中使用巨猿的现象几十年来一直在减少。
Britain banned experiments on great apes in 1986; New Zealand did so in 1999; and by 2010, the EU had outlawed all great ape research.
英国于1986年禁止对巨猿进行实验；新西兰于1999年禁止；到2010年，欧盟已宣布所有巨猿研究为非法。

Singer noted in 2006 that “no European medical research [was] currently being conducted on great apes,” since the only chimp lab in the EU (in the Netherlands) had just been shut down for lack of necessity.
Singer在2006年指出，“欧洲目前没有对大猩猩进行医学研究”，因为欧盟(荷兰)唯一的黑猩猩实验室因没有必要而刚刚关闭。
In the United States as well, the National Institutes of Health decided to retire most research chimps by the 2010s.
在美国，国家卫生研究所也决定在2010年代之前使大多数研究黑猩猩退休。

Given these trends, Singer argues that banning ape experiments is scientifically acceptable, and in any case the moral imperative of protecting our “evolutionary cousins” outweighs any extremely remote scenarios.
鉴于这些趋势，Singer认为，禁止类人猿实验在科学上是可以接受的，无论如何，保护我们的“革命堂兄弟”的道义责任大于任何极其遥远的情况。
He also clarifies that recognizing apes’ rights would not mean ending all captivity or human care.
他还澄清说，承认猿人的权利并不意味着结束所有被囚禁或人类照料。
Apes born in zoos wouldn’t simply be released into the wild to die; rather, they would be treated more like wards under human guardianship, much as incapacitated humans have guardians.
在动物园出生的猩猩不会被放入野外去死去；相反，他们将更像被人类监护的病房，更像无行为能力的人有监护人。
The aim is to stop treating great apes as mere property.
目的是停止把巨猿当作单纯的财产对待。
As Singer puts it, “Today, great apes are property…they are the closest things now existing to slaves… It is time to put the slavery of the apes behind us.”
像歌手所说"，今天，大子是财产...他们是目前与奴隶最接近的东西...

paragraphs.brief: 这场辩论正在进行中，但它强调了承认猿的权利如何能改变我们保护野生动物的方法 — — 也许可以把“权利”的概念从伦理领域扩大到生态领域。
sentences: The push for great ape rights raises profound questions about how we draw our species boundaries in law and morality.
追求大猩猩权利引起了深刻的疑问我们如何在法律和道德上划定我们的物种界限
It forces us to ask what qualities confer basic rights – is it membership in the human species, or is it intelligence, self-awareness, the capacity to suffer, or something else?
它迫使我们问，什么品质赋予基本权利？它是否属于人类，或者它是否智力、自我意识、受苦的能力或其他东西？
If societies accept that certain non-humans deserve legal rights, that could pave the way for rethinking the status of many other animals in captivity, entertainment, or agriculture.
如果社会承认某些非人类的人理应享有合法权利，那可以为重新思考许多其他被囚禁、娱乐或农业动物的地位铺平道路。
Some conservationists have even speculated that granting legal rights to wild great apes might inadvertently strengthen efforts to protect them.
有些保护者甚至猜测，给予野生巨猿合法权利可能会无意中加强保护它们的努力。

For instance, if wild orangutans or gorillas are legally seen as “persons” with a right to life and habitat, governments might be obliged to crack down harder on poaching, illegal wildlife trade, and deforestation in ape habitats.
例如，如果野生猩猩或大猩猩在法律上被视为享有生命和生境权的“人”，政府可能不得不更严厉地打击偷猎、非法野生动物贸易和猿类生境的森林砍伐。
In this view, an “ape rights” approach could complement traditional conservation, adding moral and legal weight to saving these species from extinction.
这种观点认为，“类人猿权利”办法可以补充传统的养护，增加道德和法律的份量，使这些物种免于灭绝。
Others caution, however, that focusing on individual rights might conflict with species-level conservation priorities or rural human communities’ needs.
然而，另一些人告诫说，注重个人权利可能与物种一级的保护优先事项或农村人类社区的需要相冲突。

This debate is ongoing, but it underlines how recognizing ape rights could transform our approach to wildlife protection – perhaps extending the concept of “rights” from the realm of ethics into ecology.
这场辩论正在进行中，但它强调了承认猿的权利如何能改变我们保护野生动物的方法 — — 也许可以把“权利”的概念从伦理领域扩大到生态领域。

paragraphs.brief: 像Singer这样的支持者坚持说，我们与猿人共有的品质要求我们扩大我们的关切范围 — — 仅仅因为猿人不是人类就剥夺他们的权利就是不公正的“物种 ”。
sentences: In summary, the idea of extending legal personhood and basic rights to great apes has moved from a fringe proposal to a topic of serious discussion over the past 30 years.
简言之，将法人地位和基本权利扩大到巨猿的想法，在过去30年中从一个边缘性建议转向一个认真讨论的议题。
It has seen some success (like New Zealand’s and Spain’s actions) and sparked intense philosophical debate.
它取得了一些成功(如新西兰和西班牙的行动)，并引发了激烈的哲学辩论。
Supporters like Singer insist that our shared qualities with apes demand we broaden our circle of concern – denying apes rights purely because they’re not human is unjust “speciesism.”
像Singer这样的支持者坚持说，我们与猿人共有的品质要求我们扩大我们的关切范围 — — 仅仅因为猿人不是人类就剥夺他们的权利就是不公正的“物种 ”。
Critics – from religious leaders to humanist organizations – respond that human rights should be secured first and that we risk erasing the unique moral line separating humans from animals.
批评者 — — 从宗教领袖到人道主义组织 — — 的反应是，人权应该首先得到保障，我们有可能消除将人类与动物分开的独特道德界限。
There are also practical worries about impacts on research and societal values.
对于研究和社会价值的影响，也存在着实际的担忧。

As of now, great apes remain legal property in most of the world, without rights, but the Great Ape Project’s campaign has at least succeeded in forcing people to confront the question: If not humans, who else merits basic rights?
目前，大猩猩在世界大部分地区仍拥有合法财产，没有权利，但大猩猩项目运动至少成功地迫使人们面对这个问题：如果不是人类，谁应该享有基本权利？
And if chimpanzees do, then perhaps our ethical community is not a humans-only club after all.
如果黑猩猩这样做，那么也许我们的伦理界毕竟不是一个只属于人类的俱乐部。

This ongoing conversation – described in Peter Singer’s 2006 Guardian article and echoed in news reports and critiques of the time – represents “a significant step forwards” in humanity’s ever-expanding moral evolution.
